stem.en: A tanker on the high seas has oily waste on board, and no coast is in sight. What is the right action?

text.en: Put it overboard, as no country owns the water.

feedback.en: Ships are prohibited from polluting the seas, and that holds on the high seas too.

text.en: Put it overboard, as it is beyond 200 nautical miles.

feedback.en: Distance from the coast does not free a ship from the rule, and the current can carry oil a long way.

text.en: Keep it on board and hand it over at a port.

feedback.en: Yes. Ships are prohibited from polluting the seas, so the waste stays on board until a port facility takes it.

text.en: Put it overboard, if no other ship can see it.

feedback.en: Being seen is not the test. The pollution is the same either way.

explanation.en: Ships are prohibited from polluting the seas, and MARPOL is the agreement aimed at reducing pollution from ships. Oily waste should not be dumped: it stays on board and is handed over at a port facility. Being far from land does not change this.

hints.en: Does the rule depend on who owns the water?
Where can oily waste go safely?
